title: Hash browns
subtitle: Shredded potato cakes fried in butter until crisp and golden
excerpt: Hash browns are grated raw potato squeezed of moisture, seasoned, and pressed into flat cakes in a hot buttered pan and cooked until the outside is deep golden and crisp while the inside stays tender. The key is removing as much water from the potato as possible before frying. Served alongside eggs for a classic American breakfast.
sourceNotes: American culinary tradition. Hash browns as a diner breakfast standard are documented in American cookbooks from the early twentieth century. Fannie Farmer, The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896), Project Gutenberg, describes hashed-brown potatoes as a standard breakfast preparation.

content.text: Hash browns start with raw potato grated on the coarse side of a box grater, then squeezed of as much water as possible in a clean cloth. The dry shreds fry to a crisp, golden cake rather than steaming grey. Season well and cook in a butter-and-oil combination over medium heat: butter for flavour, oil to raise the smoke point.

items.prepNote: floury variety such as Maris Piper or King Edward, peeled and coarsely grated

content.text: Grate the {{potato}} of peeled potato onto a clean cloth or several sheets of kitchen paper. Gather the cloth, twist tightly, and squeeze out as much liquid as possible over the sink. This step is important. Transfer the dry shreds to a bowl and season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat {{unsalted-butter}} of butter and {{vegetable-oil}} of oil in the frying pan over medium heat until the butter is foaming. Divide the shredded potato into 4 loose portions and press into the pan into flat cakes about 1.5 cm thick.
Cook for 6 to 7 minutes without moving. The base should be deep golden when you check. Flip carefully and cook for a further 6 minutes until the second side matches. Serve immediately.

items.fix: Squeeze twice, as hard as possible. The amount of water that comes out of a raw potato is surprising.

items.symptom: Hash browns falling apart when flipping
items.cause: Flipped before the base has set into a cohesive cake.
items.fix: Do not flip for at least 6 minutes. The crust must be fully set before it will hold together.

content.text: A small amount of grated onion mixed with the potato is the diner version. Adding a tablespoon of cornflour to the squeezed shreds helps bind them. One large hash brown for the whole pan, cut into wedges to serve, is easier to manage than individual patties.

Hash browns are a fixture of the American breakfast plate alongside eggs, bacon, and toast. The diner version, cooked on a flat griddle and served as a rectangle of crisp potato, is one of the defining American breakfast foods. The name comes from the French verb hacher, to chop or mince, referring to the shredded or diced form.
